chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the will/testament of a young boy (ghulam), is it valid? He said: 'If he is ten years old, his will is valid.'
ai.seo_question: At what age is a child's will considered valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing ten years as the age of *rushd* (prudence) for the validity of a child's will. This ruling distinguishes between mere minority and the capacity for financial discretion, allowing a boy of ten to bequeath his property, a principle foundational to Shia inheritance jurisprudence.
